evidence.basis_disclosure: all-fragments basis, n_L(C++) = 44 of 44 probes (no NONE-scored probes for C++ in this universe). Common-basis figure requires cross-language merge and is not computed by this single-language work unit.

checklist_categories: 3 overload / dynamic dispatch not locally evident
4 implicit allocation, copy, move, destruction, or cleanup
9 hidden side effects on existing state
counting_rule.definition: For each of the 44 fixed probes, author the R10-selected idiomatic C++ fragment satisfying the probe's canonical_task, then count how many of the 9 frozen hidden-behavior checklist categories are triggered by that fragment's measured_fragment text (a category counts once per probe regardless of how many times it recurs inside that probe; a behavior is NOT counted if the fixed local syntax makes it unambiguous under the C++ standard, per common.md instruction). Per-probe count ranges 0-9.
counting_rule.normalization_formula: score = 100 * (1 - sum_of_per_probe_hidden_counts / (44 probes * 9 categories)); higher score = lower hidden cost = better. Denominator (396) is fixed before measurement and identical for every language, so scores are directly comparable.
counting_rule.note_on_common_basis: This raw count was computed on the full 44-probe all-fragments basis for C++ (all 44 probes have a FULL or PARTIAL C++ fragment; C++ has no NONE probes in this universe). Common-basis (all-ten-language-fragment) recomputation is deferred to cross-language aggregation, which is outside this single-language work unit's scope; this evidence record publishes the all-fragments figure with its basis size (44) as required by interaction_with_quality_metrics.basis_reporting_requirement.

evidence.limitations: Per-probe hidden counts were authored and scored by this worker against the frozen R1-R10 authoring rules and the 9-item checklist, using standard, idiomatic clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 fragments consistent with the frozen toolchain recipe; fragments were not mechanically compiled/run in this packet-only work unit, so V1 build/run evidence is not attached here and should be reconciled with the mechanical build-verification work unit before Semantic Compression status is marked COMPLETE.
evidence.methodology_basis: semantic_compression.md section D (frozen 9-item checklist), capability_universe.json probes F01.P1..F20.P2, authoring rules R1-R10 (idiomatic C++20, clang++ -std=c++20 -O2, no checked-arithmetic mode per toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause).

F01.P1.reason: const int n=7; return n; — no ambiguous conversion, aliasing, dispatch, allocation, exception, nullability, representation change, overflow, or side effect.

F01.P2.reason: namespace-scope int64_t counter=0 / const int64_t LIMIT=100 — static storage duration implies implicit constant-initialization/destruction sequencing not visible at the two declarations (cat 4).

F02.P1.reason: int32_t v; two-way branch assigns both arms — C++ has no compiler-enforced definite-assignment check; reading v if a path were missed is UB, a failure mode not signaled by the syntax (cat 5).

F02.P2.reason: uint8_t buf[16]; local array left uninitialized — indeterminate values are stack-allocated implicitly with no init marker beyond the absent initializer (cat 4).

F03.P1.reason: x += 1 on a plain signed int — clang++ has no checked-arithmetic mode (toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause), so overflow is UB, a context-dependent numeric behavior not visible at the operator (cat 8).

F03.P2.reason: xs[1]=42 on std::vector — operator[] performs no bounds check; out-of-range is UB, a failure mode not surfaced at the site (cat 5).

F04.P1.reason: int& port=slot; port=9; — writable alias is an explicit reference declaration, fully locally evident.

F04.P2.reason: std::span<const int> window(xs) — non-copying read-only view explicit in the type.

F04.P3.reason: identity check routed through a container (e.g. std::vector<std::shared_ptr<T>>) — shared_ptr copy increments/decrements a refcount implicitly (cat 4).

F05.P1.reason: bare call f(x) where f takes std::vector<int> by value — call site cannot reveal whether the callee copies or aliases (cat 2); if by-value, an implicit full-vector copy occurs at the call boundary (cat 4).

F05.P2.reason: void put(int&x){x=12;} — explicit reference parameter, aliasing fully declared.

F05.P3.reason: lambda capturing k passed by name to std::transform — closure object construction/allocation is implicit (cat 4).

F06.P1.reason: int mid(std::vector<int> v){return v[1];} — by-value parameter implies a hidden copy at the call site (cat 4); v[1] is an unchecked, potentially-UB index (cat 5).

F06.P2.reason: std::pair<int,int> divmod2(...) with a/b and a%b — division by zero is UB, not surfaced (cat 5); structured-binding decomposition performs an implicit copy/move of each element (cat 4).

F07.P1.reason: int r=a*b+c — unchecked signed overflow is UB (cat 8).

F07.P2.reason: int q=a/b; int m=a%b; double d=(double)a/b — division-by-zero UB on q/m (cat 8); the explicit cast for d is NOT hidden.

F08.P1.reason: plain m+1 at INT_MAX (no std checked/wrapping/saturating op exists in C++20 std library; rung iv applies) — overflow is UB, both a numeric-edge behavior (cat 8) and an unsignalled failure (cat 5).

F08.P2.reason: explicit (b==0)?0:a/b guard — outcome fully locally determinate, no hidden behavior.

F09.P1.reason: s1==s2 for std::string is a statically-resolved, well-documented content comparison — not hidden dynamic dispatch.

F09.P2.reason: std::sort(xs.rbegin(),xs.rend()) and a<b — in-place mutation and ordering are explicit/well-known from the reverse-iterator idiom.

F10.P1.reason: static_cast<int32_t>(big) — pre-C++20 out-of-range narrowing to a signed type is implementation-defined; the exact truncation/wrap behavior is not fixed by the cast syntax alone (cat 7).

F10.P2.reason: double sum = i + d — int-to-double promotion of i is an implicit conversion before the addition (cat 1).

F11.P1.reason: int e = xs[i] — unchecked indexed read; out-of-range is UB, a failure not surfaced at the site (cat 5).

F11.P2.reason: std::vector<int> part(xs.begin()+1, xs.begin()+4) — range-constructor allocates a new vector and copies the three elements, an implicit allocation/copy (cat 4).

F12.P1.reason: std::optional<int32_t> o = std::nullopt; o.value_or(0) — nullability and fallback fully explicit in the type and call.

F12.P2.reason: lambda h passed to optional::transform — closure construction is an implicit allocation (cat 4).

F13.P1.reason: std::stoi(s) inside parse_twice with no declared exception spec — std::invalid_argument/out_of_range propagate implicitly, not visible in the function's declared interface (cat 5).

F13.P2.reason: catch(...) around std::stoi — catch-all obscures which specific exception types are actually thrown/handled (cat 5).

F14.P1.reason: Shape s = Circle{2.0} into std::variant<Circle,Rect> — converting-constructor selection for the active alternative is an implicit conversion (cat 1).

F14.P2.reason: std::visit(overloaded-lambda, s) — the overload actually invoked for the active alternative is resolved by the visitor mechanism, not locally evident at the call site (cat 3).

F14.P3.reason: virtual Shape::area() dispatched to Tri defined in a separate unit — vtable dispatch is not locally evident at the call site (cat 3).

F15.P1.reason: template<typename T> T head(std::vector<T> xs){return xs[0];} — by-value vector parameter implies an implicit copy per instantiation (cat 4); xs[0] is unchecked (cat 5, folded here as a second hidden category alongside the copy).

F15.P2.reason: template<typename T> requires std::totally_ordered<T> ... — C++20 concept constraint is declared explicitly at the generic's declaration.

F15.P3.reason: std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Named>> items — virtual dispatch through the base pointer is not locally evident (cat 3); unique_ptr insertion/ownership transfer is an implicit move (cat 4).

F16.P1.reason: std::accumulate(xs.begin(),xs.end(),0) — the running sum can silently overflow with no checked mode (cat 8).

F16.P2.reason: std::unordered_map iteration order is unspecified by the standard and not recoverable from the fragment's syntax (context-dependent behavior not locally evident).

F17.P1.reason: std::ifstream RAII handle — the file-close cleanup runs implicitly in the destructor at scope exit, with no explicit close() call in the fragment (cat 4).

F17.P2.reason: user-defined ~Handle(){++released;} — destructor invocation at end of block scope is an implicit, compiler-inserted call (cat 4).

F18.P1.reason: std::cout << "x" << "\n" — operator<< is overload-resolved against std::ostream's overload set, not enumerable purely from the call site (cat 3).

F18.P2.reason: util::pub_add(2,3) with secret() kept internal-linkage in the same unit — visibility boundary and qualified call are explicit.

F19.P1.reason: std::async/std::future — an exception thrown inside the async task is stored and only rethrown implicitly on future::get() (cat 5); std::async's internal thread/state allocation is implicit (cat 4).

F19.P2.reason: std::thread + std::atomic<int64_t> — a std::thread destructor calls std::terminate implicitly if joinable and not joined/detached, a hidden failure mode tied to control flow (cat 5).

F20.P1.reason: extern "C" int abs(int); — the foreign-boundary declaration is fully explicit.

F20.P2.reason: extern "C" int add2(int a,int b){return a+b;} — C-ABI export explicit via extern "C".
